questions.question: Which business structure is most commonly recommended for drone businesses?
questions.questionHtml: Which business structure is most commonly recommended for drone businesses?
questions.feedback: An LLC provides personal liability protection with simpler administration than a corporation, making it the most practical choice for most drone businesses.
questions.feedbackHtml: An LLC provides liability protection with simpler administration than a corporation.

questions.question: Select ALL that apply: What types of insurance should a drone business consider?
questions.questionHtml: Select ALL that apply: What types of insurance should a drone business consider?
questions.feedback: General liability, professional liability, and home-based business insurance are all important for drone businesses. Hull insurance covers equipment, but there is no life insurance for drones.
questions.feedbackHtml: General liability, professional liability, and home-based business insurance are all relevant for drone operators.

questions.question: Why is it critical to keep business and personal finances completely separate?
questions.questionHtml: Why is it critical to keep business and personal finances completely separate?

answers.text: It makes tax filing slightly easier
A judge could eliminate your LLC liability protection if finances are mixed
answers.textHtml: A judge could eliminate your LLC liability protection if finances are mixed

answers.text: Banks require it for all business accounts
answers.textHtml: Banks require it for all business accounts

answers.text: It is required by the FAA

questions.feedback: If personal and business finances are intermingled, a judge can pierce the corporate veil and eliminate your LLC's liability protection, exposing your personal assets.
questions.feedbackHtml: Mixing finances can cause a judge to pierce the corporate veil, eliminating your liability protection.

questions.question: Match each business structure to its liability protection level:
questions.questionHtml: Match each business structure to its liability protection level:

answers.matchText: Personal liability protection with some limits

questions.feedback: Sole proprietorships offer no protection. LLCs and S-Corps both offer limited liability protection, with S-Corps providing pass-through taxation benefits.
questions.feedbackHtml: Protection increases from sole proprietorship (none) to LLC and S-Corp (limited protection).

questions.question: What is an EIN?

answers.text: Employer Identification Number — like a Social Security Number for your business
answers.textHtml: Employer Identification Number — like a Social Security Number for your business

questions.feedback: An EIN (Employer Identification Number) is the IRS equivalent of a Social Security Number for your business. Apply for it at irs.gov.
questions.feedbackHtml: An EIN is your business's identification number with the IRS. Apply for free at irs.gov.
